chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Jamil ibn Darradj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'Is alms-tax (sadaqah) permissible for the Banu Hashim?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'Is it permissible for their mawalis (clients/followers)?' He said, 'It is permissible for their mawalis, and it is not permissible for them (Banu Hashim) except the alms of one of them given to another.'

As for the report narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Give from the zakat to the Banu Hashim whoever among them wishes, for it is permissible for them, and it is only forbidden upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and upon the Imam who comes after him and upon the Imams (peace be upon them).'

The primary narrator in this report is Abu Khadijah, and although it is repeated in the books, no one else has narrated it from him. It is possible that he (peace be upon him) meant the state of necessity rather than the state of choice, because we have clarified that in the state of necessity it is permissible for them. The reason for singling out the Imams (peace be upon them) from among them in the report is that the Imams (peace be upon them) are not compelled to consume the alms-tax and sustain themselves with it, whereas others from the Banu Abd al-Muttalib may be compelled to do so.

As for the report narrated by: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: 'I sent to al-Rida (peace be upon him) dinars from some of my family, and I wrote to him informing him that among them was zakat of seventy-five and the remainder was a gift. He wrote back in his own hand: 'I received it and sent to him dinars for me and for others.' And I wrote to him that they were from the fitrah (alms) of the dependents, so he wrote back in his own hand: 'I received it.'

Thus, in this report it is not established that he received it for himself or for others; it is possible that he received it for others who are entitled to it, because the Imams (peace be upon them) used to receive the alms-tax, seek it, and distribute it among their mawalis who are entitled to it.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: Obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Alms-giving, specifically referring to the general category of sadaqah or zakat in this context
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: Necessity or need, a legal state justifying what is otherwise restricted
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, specifically referring to the infallible Imams in this context
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: Clients or followers, often referring to non-Arabs who converted and attached themselves to an Arab tribe
key_terms.بَنُو هَاشِمٍ: The clan of Hashim, descendants of the Prophet's grandfather, to whom the Prophet belonged

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for Banu Hashim to receive zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith resolves the apparent contradiction between the general prohibition of zakat for Banu Hashim and its permissibility for their mawalis by distinguishing between the Imams' inherent status and the needs of other clan members. Shia scholars, such as Al-Tusi, interpret the restriction as applying strictly to the Imams' personal consumption, noting they are rarely in necessity, while allowing them to accept zakat on behalf of others or in cases of dire need. This distinction underscores the unique spiritual and material standing of the Ahl al-Bayt within the broader framework of Islamic charity distribution.
